Montez Sweat began his college career at Michigan State and later transferred to Mississippi State.
As a Mississippi State senior, Montez Sweat earned first-team All-America honors from the Football Writers Association of America and Sporting News.
His senior year, Montez Sweat led the Bulldogs in sacks for the second straight season and recorded 14 tackles for loss.
At the NFL Combine, Montez Sweat ran the 40-yard dash in 4.41 seconds, setting a modern combine record for defensive linemen.

excerpts:
Multiple publications listed Sweat as one of the country's top tight end recruits at Stephenson High School in Stone Mountain, Georgia. He also played defense in high school, and he made his primary position defensive end when he arrived at Michigan State in 2014.

Three years later, Sweat transferred to Mississippi State, where he became a first-team All-American for his production off the edge.

"Initially, he's an offensive guy, so I asked him if he wanted to play tight end," Mississippi State coach Joe Moorhead told NFL.com in April. "That didn't work out so well."

**5\. He could hardly be stopped in college.**

After earning first-team All-SEC honors as a junior at Mississippi State, Sweat returned for his senior season. He only raised his draft stock.

Sweat compiled 14 tackles for loss and a team-high 12 sacks, earning second team All-America honors from The Associated Press.
citations.title: Seven Things We've Learned About Montez Sweat

excerpts:
As a senior at Mississippi State, Sweat earned first-team All-America honors from the Football Writers Association of America and Sporting News, finishing as a semifinalist for the Bednarik Award, given annually to the nation's top defensive player.

Sweat led the Bulldogs in sacks for the second consecutive season, tied for sixth nationally with 11.5 sacks along with 14 tackles for a loss, which ranked second on the team. Arguably his best game came against Auburn last season, in which he tallied three sacks and a forced fumble, both of which were career highs.
citations.title: After Trade, Redskins Select Edge Montez Sweat

excerpts:
INDIANAPOLIS -- Just five weeks after wowing NFL scouts at the Reese's [Senior Bowl](http://www.nfl.com/seniorbowl) with his on-field play, Mississippi State edge rusher Montez Sweat wowed them again on Sunday, this time with a 4.41-second 40-yard dash to set a modern record (since 2003) for a defensive lineman at the NFL [Scouting Combine](http://www.nfl.com/combine) .

The previous modern record was 4.44 by Manny Lawson (2006) and Isaac Hilton (2004), per NFL Research.

Sweat, at 260 pounds, stood out most among a defensive line group that dazzled overall.

If it's unfair for speed like Sweat's to be measured with other defensive linemen, perhaps wide receivers would make for better context. A 4.41 would rate tied for eighth-best among this year's combine receivers.
